segs.e: Linked Discourses 55.1
1. At Bamboo Gate
A Wheel-Turning Monarch
At Sāvatthī.
There the Buddha … said:

segs.p: “kiñcāpi, bhikkhave, rājā cakkavattī catunnaṁ dīpānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kāretvā kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ sahabyataṁ, so tattha nandane vane accharāsaṅghaparivuto dibbehi ca pañcahi kāmaguṇehi samappito samaṅgībhūto paricāreti, so catūhi dhammehi asamannāgato, atha kho so aparimuttova nirayā aparimutto tiracchānayoniyā aparimutto pettivisayā aparimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a wheel-turning monarch were to rule as sovereign lord over these four continents. And when his body breaks up, after death, he’s reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm, in the company of the gods of the thirty-three. There he amuses himself in the Garden of Delight, escorted by a band of nymphs, and supplied and provided with the five kinds of heavenly sensual stimulation. Still, as he’s lacking four things, he’s not exempt from hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm. He’s not exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

segs.p: Kiñcāpi, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako piṇḍiyālopena yāpeti, nantakāni ca dhāreti, so catūhi dhammehi samannāgato, atha kho so parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: Now suppose a noble disciple wears rags and feeds on scraps of almsfood. Still, as they have four things, they’re exempt from hell, the animal realm, or the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’
They have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī’ti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’
They have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ—cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā’ti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.
These are the four qualities that they possess.

segs.p: Yo ca, bhikkhave, catunnaṁ dīpānaṁ paṭilābho, yo catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābho catunnaṁ dīpānaṁ paṭilābho catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ paṭilābhassa kalaṁ nāgghati soḷasin”ti.
segs.e: And, mendicants, gaining these four continents is not worth a sixteenth part of gaining these four things.”
Linked Discourses 55.2
1. At Bamboo Gate
The Objective of the Spiritual Life

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti:
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’ti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Those who have faith and ethics,
confidence, and vision of the truth,
in time arrive at happiness,
the objective of the spiritual life.”
Linked Discourses 55.3
1. At Bamboo Gate
With Dīghāvu

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena dīghāvu upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the lay follower Dīghāvu was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho dīghāvu upāsako pitaraṁ jotikaṁ gahapatiṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then he addressed his father, the householder Jotika,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, gahapati, yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena bhagavato pāde sirasā vanda:
segs.e: “Please, householder, go to the Buddha, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:

segs.p: ‘dīghāvu, bhante, upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: ‘Sir, the lay follower Dīghāvu is sick, suffering, gravely ill.
He bows with his head to your feet.’
And then say:

segs.p: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, tātā”ti kho jotiko gahapati dīghāvussa upāsakassa paṭissutvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho jotiko gahapati bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, dear,” replied Jotika. He did as Dīghāvu asked.

segs.p: “dīghāvu, bhante, upāsako ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
‘sādhu kira, bhante, bhagavā yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

segs.e: The Buddha consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena dīghāvussa upāsakassa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā dīghāvuṁ upāsakaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the lay follower Dīghāvu, sat down on the seat spread out, and said to him,

segs.p: “kacci te, dīghāvu, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, Dīghāvu, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”
“So, Dīghāvu, you should train like this:

segs.p: ‘buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato bhavissāmi—itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: ‘I will have experiential confidence in the Buddha …
the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato bhavissāmi akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi’.
segs.e: And I will have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.’
That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: “Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṁvijjante dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, these four factors of stream-entry that were taught by the Buddha are found in me, and I exhibit them.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato—itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: For I have experiential confidence in the Buddha …
the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
And I have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha tvaṁ, dīghāvu, imesu catūsu sotāpattiyaṅgesu patiṭṭhāya cha vijjābhāgiye dhamme uttari bhāveyyāsi.
segs.e: “In that case, Dīghāvu, grounded on these four factors of stream-entry you should further develop these six things that play a part in realization.

segs.p: Idha tvaṁ, dīghāvu, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharāhi, anicce dukkhasaññī, dukkhe anattasaññī pahānasaññī virāgasaññī nirodhasaññīti.
segs.e: You should meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions, perceiving suffering in impermanence, perceiving not-self in suffering, perceiving giving up, perceiving fading away, and perceiving cessation.
That’s how you should train.”

segs.p: “Yeme, bhante, bhagavatā cha vijjābhāgiyā dhammā desitā, saṁvijjante dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi.
segs.e: “These six things that play a part in realization that were taught by the Buddha are found in me, and I exhibit them.

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharāmi, anicce dukkhasaññī, dukkhe anattasaññī pahānasaññī virāgasaññī nirodhasaññī.
segs.e: For I meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions, perceiving suffering in impermanence, perceiving not-self in suffering, perceiving giving up, perceiving fading away, and perceiving cessation.

segs.p: Api ca me, bhante, evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: But still, sir, I think,

segs.p: ‘mā hevāyaṁ jotiko gahapati mamaccayena vighātaṁ āpajjī’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I hope Jotika doesn’t suffer distress when I’ve gone.’”
Jotika said, “Dear Dīghāvu, don’t focus on that.

segs.p: Iṅgha tvaṁ, tāta dīghāvu, yadeva te bhagavā āha, tadeva tvaṁ sādhukaṁ manasi karohī”ti.
segs.e: Come on, dear Dīghāvu, you should closely focus on what the Buddha is saying.”

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā dīghāvuṁ upāsakaṁ iminā ovādena ovaditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: When the Buddha had given this advice he rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho dīghāvu upāsako acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi.
segs.e: Not long after the Buddha left, Dīghāvu passed away.

segs.p: Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then several mendicants went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “yo so, bhante, dīghāvu nāma upāsako bhagavatā saṅkhittena ovādena ovadito so kālaṅkato.
segs.e: “Sir, the lay follower named Dīghāvu, who was advised in brief by the Buddha, has passed away.
Where has he been reborn in his next life?”

segs.p: “Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, dīghāvu upāsako, paccapādi dhammassānudhammaṁ, na ca maṁ dhammādhikaraṇaṁ vihesesi.
segs.e: “Mendicants, the lay follower Dīghāvu was astute. He practiced in line with the teaching, and did not trouble me about the teachings.

segs.p: Dīghāvu, bhikkhave, upāsako pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātiko tattha parinibbāyī anāvattidhammo tasmā lokā”ti.
segs.e: With the ending of the five lower fetters, he’s been reborn spontaneously, and will become extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.”
Linked Discourses 55.4
1. At Bamboo Gate
With Sāriputta (1st)

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca sāriputto āyasmā ca ānando sāvatthiyaṁ viharanti jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Ānanda came out of retreat … and said to Sāriputta:

segs.p: “katinaṁ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, dhammānaṁ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṁ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend, how many things do people have to possess in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

segs.p: “Catunnaṁ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṁ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṁ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.
segs.e: “Reverend, people have to possess four things in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idhāvuso, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imesaṁ kho, āvuso, catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ samannāgamanahetu evamayaṁ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.
segs.e: People have to possess these four things in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
Linked Discourses 55.5
1. At Bamboo Gate
With Sāriputta (2nd)

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Sāriputta went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:
“Sāriputta, they speak of a ‘factor for stream-entry’.
What is a factor for stream-entry?”

segs.p: “Sappurisasaṁsevo hi, bhante, sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, saddhammassavanaṁ sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, yonisomanasikāro sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti sotāpattiyaṅgan”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, the factors for stream-entry are associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.”
“Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Sappurisasaṁsevo hi, sāriputta, sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, saddhammassavanaṁ sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, yonisomanasikāro sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ, dhammānudhammappaṭipatti sotāpattiyaṅgaṁ.
segs.e: For the factors for stream-entry are associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.
Sāriputta, they speak of ‘the stream’.
What is the stream?”

segs.p: “Ayameva hi, bhante, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo soto, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: “Sir, the stream is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:

segs.p: sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhī”ti.
segs.e: right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.”
“Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Ayameva hi, sāriputta, ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo soto, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: For the stream is simply this noble eightfold path, that is:
right view, right purpose, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right immersion.
Sāriputta, they speak of ‘a stream-enterer’.
What is a stream-enterer?”

segs.p: “Yo hi, bhante, iminā ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato ayaṁ vuccati sotāpanno, svāyaṁ āyasmā evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, anyone who possesses this noble eightfold path is called a stream-enterer, the venerable of such name and such clan.”
“Good, good, Sāriputta!

segs.p: Yo hi, sāriputta, iminā ariyena aṭṭhaṅgikena maggena samannāgato ayaṁ vuccati sotāpanno, svāyaṁ āyasmā evaṁnāmo evaṅgotto”ti.
segs.e: For anyone who possesses this noble eightfold path is called a stream-enterer, the venerable of such name and such clan.”
Linked Discourses 55.6
1. At Bamboo Gate
The Chamberlains
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṁ karonti:
segs.e: At that time several mendicants were making a robe for the Buddha, thinking that
when his robe was finished and the three months of the rains residence had passed the Buddha would set out wandering.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena isidattapurāṇā thapatayo sādhuke paṭivasanti kenacideva karaṇīyena.
segs.e: Now at that time the chamberlains Isidatta and Purāṇa were residing in Sādhuka on some business.
They heard about this.

segs.p: Atha kho isidattapurāṇā thapatayo magge purisaṁ ṭhapesuṁ:
segs.e: So they posted someone on the road, saying:

segs.p: “yadā tvaṁ, ambho purisa, passeyyāsi bhagavantaṁ āgacchantaṁ arahantaṁ sammāsambuddhaṁ, atha amhākaṁ āroceyyāsī”ti.
segs.e: “My man, let us know when you see the Blessed One coming, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha.”

segs.p: Dvīhatīhaṁ ṭhito kho so puriso addasa bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
segs.e: And that person stood there for two or three days before they saw the Buddha coming off in the distance.

segs.p: Disvāna yena isidattapurāṇā thapatayo tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā isidattapurāṇe thapatayo etadavoca:
segs.e: When they saw him, they went to the chamberlains and said:

segs.p: “ayaṁ so, bhante, bhagavā āgacchati arahaṁ sammāsambuddho.
segs.e: “Sirs, the Blessed One, the perfected one, the fully awakened Buddha is coming.
Please come at your convenience.”

segs.p: Atha kho isidattapurāṇā thapatayo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā bhagavantaṁ piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhiṁsu.
segs.e: Then the chamberlains went up to the Buddha, bowed, and followed behind him.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā maggā okkamma yena aññataraṁ rukkhamūlaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: And then the Buddha left the road, went to the root of a certain tree, and sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu.
segs.e: The chamberlains Isidatta and Purāṇa bowed, sat down to one side,

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te isidattapurāṇā thapatayo bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: and said to the Buddha:
“Sir, when we hear that

segs.p: ‘sāvatthiyā kosalesu cārikaṁ pakkamissatī’ti, hoti no tasmiṁ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṁ:
segs.e: you will be setting out from Sāvatthī to wander in the Kosalan lands, we’re sad and upset, thinking that
you will be far from us.

segs.p: Yadā pana mayaṁ, bhante, bhagavantaṁ suṇāma:
segs.e: And when we hear that

segs.p: ‘sāvatthiyā kosalesu cārikaṁ pakkanto’ti, hoti no tasmiṁ samaye anattamanatā hoti domanassaṁ:
segs.e: you are setting out from Sāvatthī to wander in the Kosalan lands, we’re sad and upset, thinking that
you are far from us.

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, thapatayo, sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā.
segs.e: “Well then, chamberlains, life at home is cramped and dirty, life gone forth is wide open.
Just this much is enough for diligence.”

segs.p: “Atthi kho no, bhante, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, for us there is something that’s even more cramped than that, and is considered as such.”

segs.p: “Katamo pana vo, thapatayo, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti?
segs.e: “What is that?”

segs.p: “Idha mayaṁ, bhante, yadā rājā pasenadi kosalo uyyānabhūmiṁ niyyātukāmo hoti, ye te rañño pasenadissa kosalassa nāgā opavayhā te kappetvā, yā tā rañño pasenadissa kosalassa pajāpatiyo piyā manāpā tā ekaṁ purato ekaṁ pacchato nisīdāpema.
segs.e: “Sir, it’s when King Pasenadi of Kosala wants to go and visit a park. We have to harness and prepare his royal elephants. Then we have to seat his dear and beloved wives on the elephants, one in front of us, and one behind.

segs.p: Tāsaṁ kho pana, bhante, bhaginīnaṁ evarūpo gandho hoti, seyyathāpi nāma gandhakaraṇḍakassa tāvadeva vivariyamānassa, yathā taṁ rājakaññānaṁ gandhena vibhūsitānaṁ.
segs.e: Those sisters smell like a freshly opened perfume box; that’s how the royal ladies smell with makeup on.

segs.p: Tāsaṁ kho pana, bhante, bhaginīnaṁ evarūpo kāyasamphasso hoti, seyyathāpi nāma tūlapicuno vā kappāsapicuno vā, yathā taṁ rājakaññānaṁ sukhedhitānaṁ.
segs.e: The touch of those sisters is like a tuft of cotton-wool or kapok; that’s how pampered the royal ladies are.

segs.p: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhante, samaye nāgopi rakkhitabbo hoti, tāpi bhaginiyo rakkhitabbā honti, attāpi rakkhitabbo hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time we must look after the elephants, the sisters, and ourselves.

segs.p: Na kho pana mayaṁ, bhante, abhijānāma tāsu bhaginīsu pāpakaṁ cittaṁ uppādetā.
segs.e: But we don’t recall having a bad thought regarding those sisters.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho no, bhante, etamhā sambādhā añño sambādho sambādhataro ceva sambādhasaṅkhātataro cā”ti.
segs.e: This is that thing that’s even more cramped than that, and is considered as such.”

segs.p: “Tasmātiha, thapatayo, sambādho gharāvāso rajāpatho, abbhokāso pabbajjā.

segs.p: Catūhi kho, thapatayo, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, thapatayo, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: vigatamalamaccherena cetasā ajjhāgāraṁ vasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato.
segs.e: They live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Imehi kho, thapatayo, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

segs.p: Tumhe kho, thapatayo, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā—
segs.e: And you have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: yaṁ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṁ sabbaṁ taṁ appaṭivibhattaṁ sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi.
segs.e: And whatever there is in your family that’s available to give, you share it all with those who are ethical, of good character.
What do you think, chamberlains?

segs.p: katividhā te kosalesu manussā ye tumhākaṁ samasamā, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: How many people among the Kosalans are your equal
when it comes to giving and sharing?”
“We’re fortunate, sir, so very fortunate,
in that the Buddha understands us like this.”
Linked Discourses 55.7
1. At Bamboo Gate
The People of Bamboo Gate
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ yena veḷudvāraṁ nāma kosalānaṁ brāhmaṇagāmo tadavasari.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was wandering in the land of the Kosalans together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants when he arrived at a village of the Kosalan brahmins named Bamboo Gate.
The brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate heard:

segs.p: “samaṇo khalu, bho, gotamo sakyaputto sakyakulā pabbajito kosalesu cārikaṁ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ veḷudvāraṁ anuppatto.
segs.e: “It seems the ascetic Gotama—a Sakyan, gone forth from a Sakyan family—has arrived at Bamboo Gate, together with a large Saṅgha of mendicants.

segs.p: Taṁ kho pana bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ evaṁ kalyāṇo kittisaddo abbhuggato:
segs.e: He has this good reputation:

segs.p: ‘itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā’.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: So imaṁ lokaṁ sadevakaṁ samārakaṁ sabrahmakaṁ sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiṁ pajaṁ sadevamanussaṁ sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedeti.
segs.e: He has realized with his own insight this world—with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, gods and humans—and he makes it known to others.

segs.p: So dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
segs.e: He teaches Dhamma that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

segs.p: Sādhu kho pana tathārūpānaṁ arahataṁ dassanaṁ hotī”ti.
segs.e: It’s good to see such perfected ones.”

segs.p: Atha kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā appekacce bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Appekacce bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu; sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Appekacce yena bhagavā tenañjaliṁ paṇāmetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Appekacce bhagavato santike nāmagottaṁ sāvetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Appekacce tuṇhībhūtā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: Then the brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate went up to the Buddha. Before sitting down to one side, some bowed, some exchanged greetings and polite conversation, some held up their cupped palms toward the Buddha, some announced their name and clan, while some kept silent. Seated to one side they said to the Buddha:
“Worthy Gotama, these are our wishes, desires, and hopes.

segs.p: puttasambādhasayanaṁ ajjhāvaseyyāma, kāsikacandanaṁ paccanubhaveyyāma, mālāgandhavilepanaṁ dhāreyyāma, jātarūparajataṁ sādiyeyyāma, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyāma.
segs.e: We wish to live at home with our children; to use sandalwood imported from Kāsi; to wear garlands, fragrance, and makeup; and to accept gold and currency. And when our body breaks up, after death, we wish to be reborn in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no bhavaṁ gotamo amhākaṁ evaṅkāmānaṁ evaṁchandānaṁ evaṁadhippāyānaṁ tathā dhammaṁ desetu yathā mayaṁ puttasambādhasayanaṁ ajjhāvaseyyāma …pe… sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjeyyāmā”ti.
segs.e: Given that we have such wishes, may the Buddha teach us the Dhamma so that we may achieve them.”
“Householders, I will teach you an explanation of the Dhamma that is relevant for oneself.

segs.p: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bho”ti kho te veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, worthy sir,” they replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And what is the explanation of the Dhamma that applies to oneself?
It’s when a noble disciple reflects:
‘I want to live and don’t want to die; I want to be happy and recoil from pain.

segs.p: Yo kho maṁ jīvitukāmaṁ amaritukāmaṁ sukhakāmaṁ dukkhappaṭikūlaṁ jīvitā voropeyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: Since this is so, if someone were to take my life, I wouldn’t like that.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana paraṁ jīvitukāmaṁ amaritukāmaṁ sukhakāmaṁ dukkhappaṭikūlaṁ jīvitā voropeyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But others also want to live and don’t want to die; they want to be happy and recoil from pain. So if I were to take the life of someone else, they wouldn’t like that either.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo.
segs.e: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṁ paraṁ tena saṁyojeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on someone else?’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: Reflecting in this way, they give up killing living creatures themselves. And they encourage others to give up killing living creatures, praising the giving up of killing living creatures.
So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yo kho me adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyeyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to steal from me, I wouldn’t like that.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana parassa adinnaṁ theyyasaṅkhātaṁ ādiyeyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But if I were to steal from someone else, they wouldn’t like that either.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo.
segs.e: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṁ paraṁ tena saṁyojeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on someone else?’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: Reflecting in this way, they give up stealing themselves. And they encourage others to give up stealing, praising the giving up of stealing.
So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yo kho me dāresu cārittaṁ āpajjeyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to have relations with my wives, I wouldn’t like it.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana parassa dāresu cārittaṁ āpajjeyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But if I were to have relations with someone else’s wives, he wouldn’t like that either.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo.
segs.e: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by others.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṁ paraṁ tena saṁyojeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on others?’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: Reflecting in this way, they give up sexual misconduct themselves. And they encourage others to give up sexual misconduct, praising the giving up of sexual misconduct.
So their bodily behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yo kho me musāvādena atthaṁ bhañjeyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to distort my meaning by lying, I wouldn’t like it.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana parassa musāvādena atthaṁ bhañjeyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But if I were to distort someone else’s meaning by lying, they wouldn’t like it either.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo.
segs.e: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by someone else.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṁ paraṁ tena saṁyojeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on others?’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, parañca musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: Reflecting in this way, they give up lying themselves. And they encourage others to give up lying, praising the giving up of lying.
So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: “yo kho maṁ pisuṇāya vācāya mitte bhindeyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to break me up from my friends by backbiting, I wouldn’t like it.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana paraṁ pisuṇāya vācāya mitte bhindeyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ …pe…
segs.e: But if I were to break someone else from their friends by backbiting, they wouldn’t like it either. …’
So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: “yo kho maṁ pharusāya vācāya samudācareyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to attack me with harsh speech, I wouldn’t like it.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana paraṁ pharusāya vācāya samudācareyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But if I were to attack someone else with harsh speech, they wouldn’t like it either. …’
So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati:
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple reflects:

segs.p: ‘yo kho maṁ samphabhāsena samphappalāpabhāsena samudācareyya, na metaṁ assa piyaṁ manāpaṁ.
segs.e: ‘If someone were to annoy me by talking silliness and nonsense, I wouldn’t like it.

segs.p: Ahañceva kho pana paraṁ samphabhāsena samphappalāpabhāsena samudācareyyaṁ, parassapi taṁ assa appiyaṁ amanāpaṁ.
segs.e: But if I were to annoy someone else by talking silliness and nonsense, they wouldn’t like it either.’

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, parassa peso dhammo appiyo amanāpo.
segs.e: The thing that is disliked by me is also disliked by another.

segs.p: Yo kho myāyaṁ dhammo appiyo amanāpo, kathāhaṁ paraṁ tena saṁyojeyyan’ti.
segs.e: Since I dislike this thing, how can I inflict it on another?’

segs.p: So iti paṭisaṅkhāya attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṁ bhāsati.
segs.e: Reflecting in this way, they give up talking nonsense themselves. And they encourage others to give up talking nonsense, praising the giving up of talking nonsense.
So their verbal behavior is purified in three points.
And they have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti;

segs.e: the teaching …

segs.p: saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
segs.e: the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yato kho, gahapatayo, ariyasāvako imehi sattahi saddhammehi samannāgato hoti imehi catūhi ākaṅkhiyehi ṭhānehi, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple possesses these seven good qualities and these four desirable states they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto, sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, veḷudvāreyyakā brāhmaṇagahapatikā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When he had spoken, the brahmins and householders of Bamboo Gate said to the Buddha,
“Excellent, worthy Gotama! …

segs.p: ete mayaṁ bhavantaṁ gotamaṁ saraṇaṁ gacchāma dhammañca bhikkhusaṅghañca.
segs.e: We go for refuge to the worthy Gotama, to the teaching, and to the mendicant Saṅgha.

segs.p: Upāsake no bhavaṁ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupete saraṇaṁ gate”ti.
segs.e: From this day forth, may the worthy Gotama remember us as lay followers who have gone for refuge for life.”

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati rājakārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the Royal Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho sahassabhikkhunisaṅgho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho tā bhikkhuniyo bhagavā etadavoca:

segs.e: the teaching …

Linked Discourses 55.12
2. The Royal Monastery
The Brahmins
At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, the brahmins advocate a practice called ‘get up and go’.
They encourage their disciple:

segs.p: ‘ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, kālasseva uṭṭhāya pācīnamukho yāhi.
segs.e: ‘Please, my man, rising early you should face east and walk.

segs.p: So tvaṁ mā sobbhaṁ parivajjehi, mā papātaṁ, mā khāṇuṁ, mā kaṇḍakaṭhānaṁ, mā candaniyaṁ, mā oḷigallaṁ.
segs.e: Do not avoid a pit, a cliff, a stump, thorny ground, a swamp, or a sewer.
You should await death in the place that you fall.

segs.p: Evaṁ tvaṁ, ambho purisa, kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjissasī’ti.
segs.e: And when your body breaks up, after death, you’ll be reborn in a good place, a heaven realm.’

segs.p: Taṁ kho panetaṁ, bhikkhave, brāhmaṇānaṁ bālagamanametaṁ mūḷhagamanametaṁ na nibbidāya na virāgāya na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: But this practice of the brahmins is a foolish procedure, a stupid procedure. It doesn’t lead to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, or extinguishment.

segs.p: Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyassa vinaye udayagāminiṁ paṭipadaṁ paññāpemi;
segs.e: But in the training of the Noble One I advocate a ‘get up and go’ practice

segs.p: yā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṁvattati.
segs.e: which does lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.

segs.p: Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, udayagāminī paṭipadā;
segs.e: And what is that ‘get up and go’ practice?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti;

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Ayaṁ kho sā, bhikkhave, udayagāminī paṭipadā ekantanibbidāya …pe…
segs.e: This is that ‘get up and go’ practice
which does lead solely to disillusionment, dispassion, cessation, peace, insight, awakening, and extinguishment.”
Linked Discourses 55.13
2. The Royal Monastery
With the Senior Monk Ānanda

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā ca ānando āyasmā ca sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ viharanti jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the venerables Ānanda and Sāriputta were staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṁ sammodi.
segs.e: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Ānanda, and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, he sat down to one side and said to him:

segs.p: “katinaṁ kho, āvuso ānanda, dhammānaṁ pahānā, katinaṁ dhammānaṁ samannāgamanahetu, evamayaṁ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend, how many things do people have to give up and how many do they have to possess in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening?”

segs.p: “Catunnaṁ kho, āvuso, dhammānaṁ pahānā, catunnaṁ dhammānaṁ samannāgamanahetu, evamayaṁ pajā bhagavatā byākatā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇāti.
segs.e: “Reverend, people have to give up four things and possess four things in order for the Buddha to declare that they’re a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.e: They don’t have the distrust in the Buddha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati tathārūpassa buddhe aveccappasādo hoti—
segs.e: And they do have the experiential confidence in the Buddha that causes a learned noble disciple to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a good place, a heavenly realm.

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dhamme appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati tathārūpassa dhamme appasādo na hoti.
segs.e: They don’t have the distrust in the teaching that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato sutavā ariyasāvako kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā sugatiṁ saggaṁ lokaṁ upapajjati tathārūpassa dhamme aveccappasādo hoti—

‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Yathārūpena ca kho, āvuso, dussīlyena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati tathārūpassa dussīlyaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: They don’t have the unethical conduct that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Yassa kassaci, mahānāma, dīgharattaṁ saddhāparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ sīlaparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ sutaparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ cāgaparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ paññāparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ, tassa yo hi khvāyaṁ kāyo rūpī cātumahābhūtiko mātāpettikasambhavo odanakummāsūpacayo aniccucchādanaparimaddanabhedanaviddhaṁsanadhammo.

segs.p: Taṁ idheva kākā vā khādanti gijjhā vā khādanti kulalā vā khādanti sunakhā vā khādanti siṅgālā vā khādanti vividhā vā pāṇakajātā khādanti;

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, puriso sappikumbhaṁ vā telakumbhaṁ vā gambhīraṁ udakarahadaṁ ogāhitvā bhindeyya.

segs.p: Evameva kho, mahānāma, yassa kassaci dīgharattaṁ saddhāparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ …pe…

segs.e: But their mind rises up, headed for a higher place.

segs.p: Tuyhaṁ kho pana, mahānāma, dīgharattaṁ saddhāparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ …pe… paññāparibhāvitaṁ cittaṁ.
segs.e: Your mind, Mahānāma, has for a long time been imbued with faith, ethics, learning, generosity, and wisdom.

segs.p: Mā bhāyi, mahānāma, mā bhāyi, mahānāma.
segs.e: Do not fear, Mahānāma, do not fear!

3. About Sarakāni
About Sarakāni (1st)

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato hoti.
segs.e: Now at that time Sarakāni the Sakyan had passed away.
The Buddha declared that he was
a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti:
segs.e: At that, several Sakyans came together complaining, grumbling, and objecting,
“Oh lord, how incredible, how amazing!

segs.p: Ettha dāni ko na sotāpanno bhavissati.
segs.e: Who can’t become a stream-enterer these days?

segs.p: Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato;
segs.e: For the Buddha even declared Sarakāni to be a stream-enterer after he passed away.
Sarakāni was too weak for the training; he used to drink liquor.”

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him what had happened. The Buddha said:

segs.p: Tatra sudaṁ, bhante, sambahulā sakkā saṅgamma samāgamma ujjhāyanti khīyanti vipācenti—
acchariyaṁ vata, bho, abbhutaṁ vata, bho.
Ettha dāni ko na sotāpanno bhavissati.
Yatra hi nāma saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato;
“Yo so, mahānāma, dīgharattaṁ upāsako buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gato dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gato saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gato, so kathaṁ vinipātaṁ gaccheyya.
segs.e: “Mahānāma, when a lay follower has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, how could they go to the underworld?

segs.p: Yañhi taṁ, mahānāma, sammā vadamāno vadeyya:
segs.e: And if anyone should rightly be said to

segs.p: ‘dīgharattaṁ upāsako buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gato dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gato saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gato’ti, saraṇāni sakkaṁ sammā vadamāno vadeyya.
segs.e: have for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha, it’s Sarakāni the Sakyan.

segs.p: Saraṇāni, mahānāma, sakko dīgharattaṁ upāsako buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gato dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gato saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gato.
segs.e: Sarakāni the Sakyan has for a long time gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha.
How could he go to the underworld?

segs.p: Idha, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Take a certain individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, and are endowed with freedom.

segs.p: So āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom. And they live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Ayampi kho, mahānāma, puggalo parimutto nirayā parimutto tiracchānayoniyā parimutto pettivisayā parimutto apāyaduggativinipātā.
segs.e: This individual is exempt from hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. They’re exempt from places of loss, bad places, the underworld.

segs.p: Idha pana, mahānāma, ekacco puggalo buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Take another individual who has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: hāsapañño javanapañño na ca vimuttiyā samannāgato.
segs.e: They have laughing wisdom and swift wisdom, but are not endowed with freedom.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena saraṇāni sakko kālaṅkato hoti.

segs.e: And if anyone should rightly be said to

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, dukkhettaṁ dubbhūmaṁ avihatakhāṇukaṁ, bījāni cassu khaṇḍāni pūtīni vātātapahatāni asārādāni asukhasayitāni, devo ca na sammā dhāraṁ anuppaveccheyya.
segs.e: Suppose there was a barren field, a barren ground, with uncleared stumps. And you had seeds that were broken, spoiled, weather-damaged, infertile, and ill kept. And the heavens didn’t provide enough rain.

segs.p: Api nu tāni bījāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyyun”ti?
segs.e: Would those seeds grow, increase, and mature?”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, mahānāma, idha dhammo durakkhāto hoti duppavedito aniyyāniko anupasamasaṁvattaniko asammāsambuddhappavedito—
segs.e: “In the same way, take a teaching that’s badly explained and badly propounded, not emancipating, not leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is not a fully awakened Buddha.
This is what I call a barren field.

segs.p: Tasmiñca dhamme sāvako viharati dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī—
segs.e: A disciple remains in such a teaching, practicing in line with that teaching, practicing it properly, living in line with that teaching.
This is what I call a bad seed.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, mahānāma, sukhettaṁ subhūmaṁ suvihatakhāṇukaṁ, bījāni cassu akhaṇḍāni apūtīni avātātapahatāni sārādāni sukhasayitāni;
segs.e: Suppose there was a fertile field, a fertile ground, well-cleared of stumps. And you had seeds that were intact, unspoiled, not weather-damaged, fertile, and well-kept. And there’s plenty of rainfall.

segs.p: Api nu tāni bījāni vuddhiṁ virūḷhiṁ vepullaṁ āpajjeyyun”ti?
segs.e: Would those seeds grow, increase, and mature?”

segs.e: “In the same way, take a teaching that’s well explained and well propounded, emancipating, leading to peace, proclaimed by someone who is a fully awakened Buddha.

segs.p: Tasmiñca dhamme sāvako viharati dhammānudhammappaṭipanno sāmīcippaṭipanno anudhammacārī—

3. About Sarakāni
With Anāthapiṇḍika (1st)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then he addressed a man,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vanda:
segs.e: “Please, my man, go to Venerable Sāriputta, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:
‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti.
segs.e: He bows with his head to your feet.’
And then say:

segs.p: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so puriso anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Anāthapiṇḍika asked.

segs.p: So āyasmato sāriputtassa pāde sirasā vandati.
‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

segs.e: Sāriputta consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya āyasmatā ānandena pacchāsamaṇena yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā sāriputto anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Sāriputta robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went with Venerable Ānanda as his second monk to Anāthapiṇḍika’s home. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Anāthapiṇḍika,

segs.p: “kacci te, gahapati, khamanīyaṁ kacci yāpanīyaṁ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, householder; I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ, na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

segs.p: “Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, buddhe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati tathārūpo te buddhe appasādo natthi.
segs.e: “Householder, you don’t have the distrust in the Buddha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, buddhe aveccappasādo—
segs.e: And you have experiential confidence in the Buddha:

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Tañca pana te buddhe aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the Buddha, that pain may die down on the spot.

segs.p: Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, dhamme appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te dhamme appasādo natthi.
segs.e: You don’t have the distrust in the teaching that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, dhamme aveccappasādo—
segs.e: And you have experiential confidence in the teaching:

segs.p: svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhīti.
segs.e: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’

segs.p: Tañca pana te dhamme aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the teaching, that pain may die down on the spot.

segs.p: Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, saṅghe appasādena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te saṅghe appasādo natthi.
segs.e: You don’t have the distrust in the Saṅgha that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, saṅghe aveccappasādo—
segs.e: And you have experiential confidence in the Saṅgha:

segs.p: suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
segs.e: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, and worthy of veneration with cupped palms. It is the supreme field of merit for the world.’

segs.p: Tañca pana te saṅghe aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that experiential confidence in the Saṅgha, that pain may die down on the spot.

segs.p: Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, dussīlyena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpaṁ te dussīlyaṁ natthi.
segs.e: You don’t have the unethical conduct that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, ariyakantāni sīlāni … pe samādhisaṁvattanikāni.
segs.e: Your ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Tāni ca pana te ariyakantāni sīlāni attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, that pain may die down on the spot.

segs.p: Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchādiṭṭhi natthi.
segs.e: You don’t have the wrong view that causes an unlearned ordinary person to be reborn—when their body breaks up, after death—in a place of loss, a bad place, the underworld, hell.

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammādiṭṭhi.
segs.e: You have right view.

segs.p: Tañca pana te sammādiṭṭhiṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that right view, that pain may die down on the spot.

segs.p: Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāsaṅkappena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāsaṅkappo natthi.
segs.e: You don’t have the wrong purpose …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsaṅkappo.
Tañca pana te sammāsaṅkappaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchāvācāya samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāvācā natthi.
segs.e: wrong speech …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvācā.
Tañca pana te sammāvācaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchākammantena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchākammanto natthi.
segs.e: wrong action …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammākammanto.
Tañca pana te sammākammantaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāājīvena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāājīvo natthi.
segs.e: wrong livelihood …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāājīvo.
Tañca pana te sammāājīvaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāvāyāmena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāvāyāmo natthi.
segs.e: wrong effort …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvāyāmo.
Tañca pana te sammāvāyāmaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchāsatiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāsati natthi.
segs.e: wrong mindfulness …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsati.
Tañca pana te sammāsatiṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāsamādhinā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpo te micchāsamādhi natthi.
segs.e: wrong immersion …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāsamādhi.
Tañca pana te sammāsamādhiṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpena kho, gahapati, micchāñāṇena samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpaṁ te micchāñāṇaṁ natthi.
segs.e: wrong knowledge …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāñāṇaṁ.
Tañca pana te sammāñāṇaṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyya.
Yathārūpāya kho, gahapati, micchāvimuttiyā samannāgato assutavā puthujjano kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā apāyaṁ duggatiṁ vinipātaṁ nirayaṁ upapajjati, tathārūpā te micchāvimutti natthi.
segs.e: wrong freedom …

segs.p: Atthi ca kho te, gahapati, sammāvimutti.
segs.e: You have right freedom.

segs.p: Tañca pana te sammāvimuttiṁ attani samanupassato ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambheyyā”ti.
segs.e: Seeing in yourself that right freedom, that pain may die down on the spot.”

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa ṭhānaso vedanā paṭippassambhiṁsu.
segs.e: And then Anāthapiṇḍika’s pain died down on the spot.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmantañca sāriputtaṁ āyasmantañca ānandaṁ sakeneva thālipākena parivisi.
segs.e: Then he served Sāriputta and Ānanda from his own dish.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhuttāviṁ onītapattapāṇiṁ aññataraṁ nīcāsanaṁ gahetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
segs.e: When Sāriputta had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, Anāthapiṇḍika took a low seat and sat to one side.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ āyasmā sāriputto imāhi gāthāhi anumodi:
segs.e: Venerable Sāriputta expressed his appreciation to him with these verses.
“Whoever has faith in the Realized One,
unwavering and well grounded;
whose ethical conduct is good,
praised and loved by the noble ones;
who has confidence in the Saṅgha,
and correct view:
they’re said to be prosperous,
their life is not in vain.
So let the wise devote themselves
to faith, ethical behaviour,
confidence, and insight into the teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ imāhi gāthāhi anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
segs.e: After expressing his appreciation to Anāthapiṇḍika with these verses, Sāriputta rose from his seat and left.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him,

segs.p: “handa kuto nu tvaṁ, ānanda, āgacchasi divādivassā”ti?
segs.e: “So, Ānanda, where are you coming from in the middle of the day?”

segs.p: “Āyasmatā, bhante, sāriputtena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati iminā ca iminā ca ovādena ovadito”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta advised the householder Anāthapiṇḍika in this way and that.”
“Sāriputta is astute, Ānanda.

segs.p: mahāpañño, ānanda, sāriputto, yatra hi nāma cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni dasahākārehi vibhajissatī”ti.
segs.e: He has great wisdom, since he can analyze the four factors of stream-entry in ten respects.”
Linked Discourses 55.27
3. About Sarakāni
With Anāthapiṇḍika (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
segs.e: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati aññataraṁ purisaṁ āmantesi:
segs.e: Then he addressed a man,

segs.p: “ehi tvaṁ, ambho purisa, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkama; upasaṅkamitvā mama vacanena āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vanda:
segs.e: “Please, my man, go to Venerable Ānanda, and in my name bow with your head to his feet. Say to him:
‘Sir, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika is sick, suffering, gravely ill.

segs.p: So āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandatī’ti.
segs.e: He bows with his head to your feet.’
And then say:

segs.p: ‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.
segs.e: ‘Sir, please visit him at his home out of sympathy.’”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho so puriso anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa paṭissutvā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so puriso āyasmantaṁ ānandaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” that man replied. He did as Anāthapiṇḍika asked.

segs.p: So āyasmato ānandassa pāde sirasā vandati.
‘sādhu kira, bhante, āyasmā ānando yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’”ti.

segs.e: Ānanda consented with silence.

segs.p: Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho āyasmā ānando anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Venerable Ānanda robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of the householder Anāthapiṇḍika. He sat down on the seat spread out and said to Anāthapiṇḍika,

segs.p: “kacci te, gahapati, khamanīyaṁ, kacci yāpanīyaṁ? Kacci dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
segs.e: “I hope you’re keeping well, householder, I hope you’re all right. I hope your pain is fading, not growing; that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

segs.p: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. My pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

segs.p: “Catūhi kho, gahapati, dhammehi samannāgatassa assutavato puthujjanassa hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: “Householder, when an unlearned ordinary person has four things, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano buddhe appasādena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: Firstly, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the Buddha.

segs.p: Tañca panassa buddhe appasādaṁ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing in themselves that distrust of the Buddha, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano dhamme appasādena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the teaching …

segs.p: Tañca panassa dhamme appasādaṁ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano saṅghe appasādena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person distrusts the Saṅgha …

segs.p: Tañca panassa saṅghe appasādaṁ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, assutavā puthujjano dussīlyena samannāgato hoti.
segs.e: Furthermore, an unlearned ordinary person has unethical conduct.

segs.p: Tañca panassa dussīlyaṁ attani samanupassato hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing in themselves that unethical conduct, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

segs.p: Imehi kho, gahapati, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatassa assutavato puthujjanassa hoti uttāso, hoti chambhitattaṁ, hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: When an unlearned ordinary person has these four things, they’re frightened and terrified, and fear what awaits them after death.

segs.p: Catūhi kho, gahapati, dhammehi samannāgatassa sutavato ariyasāvakassa na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: When a learned noble disciple has four things, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
Tañca panassa buddhe aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing in themselves that experiential confidence in the Buddha, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

segs.p: svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhīti.
Tañca panassa dhamme aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Saṅgha …

segs.p: suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
Tañca panassa saṅghe aveccappasādaṁ attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
Puna caparaṁ, gahapati, sutavā ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.

segs.p: Tāni ca panassa ariyakantāni sīlāni attani samanupassato na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayaṁ.
segs.e: Seeing in themselves that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.

segs.p: Imehi kho, gahapati, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatassa sutavato ariyasāvakassa na hoti uttāso, na hoti chambhitattaṁ, na hoti samparāyikaṁ maraṇabhayan”ti.
segs.e: When a learned noble disciple has these four things, they’re not frightened or terrified, and don’t fear what awaits them after death.”
“Honorable Ānanda, I am not afraid.
What have I to fear?

segs.p: Ahañhi, bhante, buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato homi—
segs.e: For I have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.
Yāni cimāni, bhante, bhagavatā gihisāmīcikāni sikkhāpadāni desitāni, nāhaṁ tesaṁ kiñci attani khaṇḍaṁ samanupassāmī”ti.
segs.e: And of the training rules appropriate for laypeople taught by the Buddha, I don’t see any that I have broken.”
“You’re fortunate, householder, so very fortunate!
You have declared the fruit of stream-entry.”
Linked Discourses 55.28
3. About Sarakāni
Fears and Enmities (1st)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:

segs.p: “yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni ca honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: “Householder, when a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’

segs.p: Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti?
segs.e: What are the five fears and enmities they have quelled?

segs.p: Yaṁ, gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātappaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyati.
segs.e: Anyone who kills living creatures brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from killing living creatures.
Anyone who steals …
Anyone who commits sexual misconduct …
Anyone who lies …

segs.p: yaṁ, gahapati, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānappaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, samparāyikampi bhayaṁ veraṁ pasavati, cetasikampi dukkhaṁ domanassaṁ paṭisaṁvediyati.
segs.e: Anyone who consumes beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants brims with fear and enmity both in this life and in lives to come, and experiences mental pain and sadness.

segs.p: Surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṁ taṁ bhayaṁ veraṁ vūpasantaṁ hoti.
segs.e: So that fear and enmity is quelled for anyone who refrains from beer, wine, and liquor intoxicants.

segs.p: Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.
segs.e: These are the five fears and enmities they have quelled.
What are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.
These are the four factors of stream-entry that they possess.

segs.p: Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho?
segs.e: And what is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom?

segs.p: Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako paṭiccasamuppādaññeva sādhukaṁ yoniso manasi karoti—
segs.e: A noble disciple rationally applies the mind to dependent origination itself:

segs.p: iti imasmiṁ sati idaṁ hoti, imassuppādā idaṁ uppajjati;
segs.e: ‘So, when this exists, this comes to be; due to the arising of this, this arises.

segs.p: iti imasmiṁ asati idaṁ na hoti, imassa nirodhā idaṁ nirujjhati;
segs.e: So, when this doesn’t exist, this doesn’t come to be; due to the cessation of this, this ceases. That is:

Ignorance is a requirement for choices. Choices are a requirement for consciousness. Consciousness is a requirement for name and form. Name and form are requirements for the six sense fields. The six sense fields are requirements for contact. Contact is a requirement for feeling. Feeling is a requirement for craving. Craving is a requirement for grasping. Grasping is a requirement for continued existence. Continued existence is a requirement for rebirth. Rebirth is a requirement for old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress to come to be.
That is how this entire mass of suffering originates.

When ignorance fades away and ceases no residue left behind, choices cease. When choices cease, consciousness ceases. When consciousness ceases, name and form cease. When name and form cease, the six sense fields cease. When the six sense fields cease, contact ceases. When contact ceases, feeling ceases. When feeling ceases, craving ceases. When craving ceases, grasping ceases. When grasping ceases, continued existence ceases. When continued existence ceases, rebirth ceases. When rebirth ceases, old age and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress cease.
That is how this entire mass of suffering ceases.’

segs.p: Ayamassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.
segs.e: This is the noble system that they have clearly seen and penetrated with wisdom.

segs.p: Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho. So ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṁ byākareyya:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has quelled five fears and enmities, possesses the four factors of stream-entry, and has clearly seen and penetrated the noble system with wisdom, they may, if they wish, declare of themselves:

segs.p: ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’”ti.
segs.e: ‘I’ve finished with rebirth in hell, the animal realm, and the ghost realm. I’ve finished with all places of loss, bad places, the underworld. I am a stream-enterer! I’m not liable to be reborn in the underworld, and am assured, destined for awakening.’”

3. About Sarakāni
With Nandaka the Licchavi

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

segs.p: Atha kho nandako licchavimahāmatto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho nandakaṁ licchavimahāmattaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Nandaka the Licchavi chief minister went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to him:

segs.p: “Catūhi kho, nandaka, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: “Nandaka, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, nandaka, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi kho, nandaka, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.

segs.p: Imehi ca pana, nandaka, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako āyunā saṁyutto hoti dibbenapi mānusenapi;
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is endowed with long life, both human and heavenly …
beauty …
happiness …
glory …
and sovereignty, both human and heavenly.

segs.p: Taṁ kho panāhaṁ, nandaka, nāññassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā sutvā vadāmi. Api ca yadeva mayā sāmaṁ ñātaṁ sāmaṁ diṭṭhaṁ sāmaṁ viditaṁ, tadevāhaṁ vadāmī”ti.
segs.e: Now, I don’t say this because I’ve heard it from some other ascetic or brahmin. I only say it because I’ve known, seen, and realized it for myself.”

segs.p: Evaṁ vutte, aññataro puriso nandakaṁ licchavimahāmattaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: When he had spoken, a certain person said to Nandaka:
“Sir, it is time to bathe.”
“Enough now, lad, with that exterior bath.
This interior bathing will do for me, that is,
confidence in the Buddha.”

4. Overflowing Merit
