At Sāvatthī.
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: This is the first kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …

segs.p: svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo …pe… paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhīti.

segs.e: This is the second kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Saṅgha …

segs.p: suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassāti.

segs.e: This is the third kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, a noble disciple’s ethical conduct is loved by the noble ones, unbroken, impeccable, spotless, and unmarred, liberating, praised by sensible people, not mistaken, and leading to immersion.
This is the fourth kind of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā kusalābhisandā sukhassāhārā”ti.

4. Overflowing Merit
In Common With the Gods

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgataṁ attamanā devā sabhāgataṁ kathenti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when someone possesses four things the gods are pleased and speak of what they have in common.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple possesses experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
Yā tā devatā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā ito cutā tatrūpapannā tāsaṁ evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: There are deities who possess experiential confidence in the Buddha who passed away from here and were reborn there. They think:

segs.p: ‘yathārūpena kho mayaṁ buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā tato cutā idhūpapannā, ariyasāvakopi tathārūpena buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato ehīti devānaṁ santike’ti.
segs.e: ‘Possessing such experiential confidence in the Buddha, we passed away from there and were reborn here. That noble disciple possesses the same kind of experiential confidence in the Buddha, so they will come into the presence of the gods.’
Furthermore, a noble disciple possesses experiential confidence in the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they possess the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Yā tā devatā ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā ito cutā tatrūpapannā tāsaṁ evaṁ hoti:
segs.e: There are deities who possess the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones who passed away from here and were reborn there. They think:

segs.p: ‘yathārūpehi kho mayaṁ ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā tato cutā idhūpapannā, ariyasāvakopi tathārūpehi ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato ehīti devānaṁ santike’ti.
segs.e: ‘Possessing such ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, we passed away from there and were reborn here. That noble disciple possesses the same kind of ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, so they will come into the presence of the gods.’

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgataṁ attamanā devā sabhāgataṁ kathentī”ti.
segs.e: When someone possesses four things the gods are pleased and speak of what they have in common.”

4. Overflowing Merit
With Mahānāma

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Mahānāma the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“Sir, how is a lay follower defined?”

segs.p: “Yato kho, mahānāma, buddhaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti, dhammaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti, saṅghaṁ saraṇaṁ gato hoti—
segs.e: “Mahānāma, when you’ve gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the Saṅgha,
you’re considered to be a lay follower.”
“But how is an ethical lay follower defined?”

segs.p: “Yato kho, mahānāma, upāsako pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, surāmerayamajjappamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato hoti—
segs.e: “When a lay follower doesn’t kill living creatures, steal, commit sexual misconduct, lie, or consume intoxicants of beer, wine, and liquor,

segs.p: ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako sīlasampanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: they’re considered to be an ethical lay follower.”
“But how is a faithful lay follower defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako saddho hoti, saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṁ—
segs.e: “It’s when a lay follower has faith in the Realized One’s awakening:

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’

segs.p: Ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako saddhāsampanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: Then they’re considered to be a faithful lay follower.”
“But how is a generous lay follower defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato—
segs.e: “It’s when a lay follower lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako cāgasampanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: Then they’re considered to be a generous lay follower.”
“But how is a wise lay follower defined?”

segs.p: “Idha, mahānāma, upāsako paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā—
segs.e: “It’s when a lay follower is wise. They have the wisdom of arising and passing away which is noble, penetrative, and leads to the complete ending of suffering.

segs.p: ettāvatā kho, mahānāma, upāsako paññāsampanno hotī”ti.
segs.e: Then they’re considered to be a wise lay follower.”
Linked Discourses 55.38
4. Overflowing Merit
Rain

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṁ udakaṁ yathāninnaṁ pavattamānaṁ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti, pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti, kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe paripūrenti, mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti, kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti, mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṁ paripūrenti;
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose the heavens rain heavily on a mountain top, and the water flows downhill to fill the hollows, crevices, and creeks. As they become full, they fill up the pools. The pools fill up the lakes, the lakes fill up the streams, and the streams fill up the rivers. And as the rivers become full, they fill up the ocean.

segs.p: evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa yo ca buddhe aveccappasādo, yo ca dhamme aveccappasādo, yo ca saṅghe aveccappasādo, yāni ca ariyakantāni sīlāni—

4. Overflowing Merit
With Kāḷigodhā

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā pubbaṇhasamayaṁ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena kāḷigodhāya sākiyāniyā nivesanaṁ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi.
segs.e: Then the Buddha robed up in the morning and, taking his bowl and robe, went to the home of Kāḷigodhā the Sakyan lady, where he sat down on the seat spread out.

segs.p: Atha kho kāḷigodhā sākiyānī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho kāḷigodhaṁ sākiyāniṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Kāḷigodhā went up to the Buddha, bowed, and sat down to one side. The Buddha said to her:

segs.p: “Catūhi kho, godhe, dhammehi samannāgatā ariyasāvikā sotāpannā hoti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā.
segs.e: “Godhā, a female noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, godhe, ariyasāvikā buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgatā hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a female noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvasati muttacāgā payatapāṇinī vossaggaratā yācayogā dānasaṁvibhāgaratā.
segs.e: And she lives at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share.

segs.p: Imehi kho, godhe, catūhi dhammehi samannāgatā ariyasāvikā sotāpannā hoti avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā”ti.
segs.e: A female noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”

segs.p: “Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṁvijjante dhammā mayi, ahañca tesu dhammesu sandissāmi.
segs.e: “Sir, these four factors of stream-entry that were taught by the Buddha are found in me, and I exhibit them.
For I have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: yaṁ kho pana kiñci kule deyyadhammaṁ sabbaṁ taṁ appaṭivibhattaṁ sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehī”ti.
segs.e: And I share without reservation all the gifts available to give in our family with those who are ethical and of good character.”
“You’re fortunate, Godhā, so very fortunate,
You have declared the fruit of stream-entry.”

4. Overflowing Merit
Nandiya the Sakyan

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho nandiyo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho nandiyo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then Nandiya the Sakyan went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

segs.p: “yasseva nu kho, bhante, ariyasāvakassa cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni sabbena sabbaṁ sabbathā sabbaṁ natthi sveva nu kho, bhante, ariyasāvako pamādavihārī”ti.
segs.e: “Sir, if a noble disciple were to totally and utterly lack the four factors of stream-entry, would they live negligently?”

segs.p: “‘Yassa kho, nandiya, cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni sabbena sabbaṁ sabbathā sabbaṁ natthi tamahaṁ bāhiro puthujjanapakkhe ṭhito’ti vadāmi.
segs.e: “Nandiya, someone who totally and utterly lacks these four factors of stream-entry stands outside in the faction of ordinary persons, I say.

segs.p: Api ca, nandiya, yathā ariyasāvako pamādavihārī ceva hoti, appamādavihārī ca
segs.e: Neverthless, Nandiya, as to how a noble disciple lives negligently and how they live diligently,

segs.p: taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho nandiyo sakko bhagavato paccassosi.
segs.e: “Yes, sir,” Nandiya replied.
The Buddha said this:
“And how does a noble disciple live negligently?

segs.p: Idha, nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
So tena buddhe aveccappasādena santuṭṭho na uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya, rattiṁ paṭisallānāya.
segs.e: They’re content with that confidence, and don’t make a further effort for solitude by day or retreat by night.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ pamattassa viharato pāmojjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: When they live negligently, there’s no joy.
When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.
When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.
When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.
When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.
Because principles have not become clear, they’re reckoned to live negligently.
Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: So tehi ariyakantehi sīlehi santuṭṭho na uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṁ paṭisallānāya.
segs.e: They’re content with that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, and don’t make a further effort for solitude by day or retreat by night.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ pamattassa viharato pāmojjaṁ na hoti.
segs.e: When they live negligently, there’s no joy.
When there’s no joy, there’s no rapture.
When there’s no rapture, there’s no tranquility.
When there’s no tranquility, there’s suffering.
When one is suffering, the mind does not become immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is not immersed in samādhi, principles do not become clear.
Because principles have not become clear, they’re reckoned to live negligently.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, nandiya, ariyasāvako pamādavihārī hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a noble disciple lives negligently.
And how does a noble disciple live diligently?

segs.p: Idha, nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: Firstly, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
So tena buddhe aveccappasādena asantuṭṭho uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṁ paṭisallānāya.
segs.e: But they’re not content with that confidence, and make a further effort for solitude by day and retreat by night.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ appamattassa viharato pāmojjaṁ jāyati.
segs.e: When they live diligently, joy springs up.
Being joyful, rapture springs up.
When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.
When the mind is immersed in samādhi, principles become clear.
Because principles have become clear, they’re reckoned to live diligently.
Furthermore, a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: So tehi ariyakantehi sīlehi asantuṭṭho uttari vāyamati divā pavivekāya rattiṁ paṭisallānāya.
segs.e: But they’re not content with that ethical conduct loved by the noble ones, and make a further effort for solitude by day and retreat by night.

segs.p: Tassa evaṁ appamattassa viharato pāmojjaṁ jāyati.
segs.e: When they live diligently, joy springs up.
Being joyful, rapture springs up.
When the mind is full of rapture, the body becomes tranquil.
When the body is tranquil, they feel bliss.
And when blissful, the mind becomes immersed in samādhi.

Because principles have become clear, they’re reckoned to live diligently.

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, nandiya, ariyasāvako appamādavihārī hotī”ti.
segs.e: That’s how a noble disciple lives diligently.”

5. Overflowing Merit, With Verses
Overflowing Merit (1st)
“Mendicants, there are these four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: Furthermore, they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion. …

segs.p: Ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro puññābhisandā, kusalābhisandā, sukhassāhārā.
segs.e: These are the four kinds of overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurture happiness.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
segs.e: When a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that
this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.

segs.p: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, mahāsamudde na sukaraṁ udakassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
segs.e: It’s like trying to count how much water is in the ocean. It’s not easy to say

segs.p: ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasahassānī’ti vā ‘ettakāni udakāḷhakasatasahassānī’ti vāti.
segs.e: how many gallons, how many hundreds, thousands, hundreds of thousands of gallons there are.

segs.p: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāudakakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchati.
segs.e: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of water.

segs.p: Evameva kho, bhikkhave, imehi catūhi puññābhisandehi kusalābhisandehi samannāgatassa ariyasāvakassa na sukaraṁ puññassa pamāṇaṁ gaṇetuṁ:
segs.e: In the same way, when a noble disciple has these four kinds of overflowing merit and goodness, it’s not easy to count how much merit they have by saying that
this is the extent of their overflowing merit, overflowing goodness that nurtures happiness.

segs.p: Atha kho asaṅkhyeyyo appameyyo mahāpuññakkhandhotveva saṅkhyaṁ gacchatī”ti.
segs.e: It’s simply reckoned as an incalculable, immeasurable, great mass of merit.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Hosts of people use the rivers,

all reach the great deep, the boundless ocean,
the cruel sea that’s home to precious gems.

and they’re a giver of beds, seats, and mats—
the streams of merit reach that astute person,
as the rivers bring their waters to the sea.”

segs.e: “Nandiya, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, nandiya, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi kho, nandiya, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
Linked Discourses 55.48
5. Overflowing Merit, With Verses
With Bhaddiya
At Kapilavatthu.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho bhaddiyaṁ sakkaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to Bhaddiya the Sakyan:

segs.p: “catūhi kho, bhaddiya, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: “Bhaddiya, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer …”

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
Imehi kho, bhaddiya, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 55.49
5. Overflowing Merit, With Verses
With Mahānāma
At Kapilavatthu.

segs.p: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho mahānāmaṁ sakkaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: Seated to one side, the Buddha said to Mahānāma the Sakyan:

segs.p: “catūhi kho, mahānāma, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti …pe… sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: “Mahānāma, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer …”

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
Imehi kho, mahānāma, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.

segs.e: Linked Discourses 55.50
5. Overflowing Merit, With Verses
Factors
“Mendicants, there are these four factors for stream-entry.
What four?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.
These are the four factors for stream-entry.”
Linked Discourses 55.51
6. A Wise Person
With Verses

segs.p: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo.
segs.e: “Mendicants, a noble disciple who has four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.
What four?

segs.p: Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti—
segs.e: It’s when a noble disciple has experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehi.
segs.e: And they have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.

segs.p: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato ariyasāvako sotāpanno hoti avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti.
segs.e: A noble disciple who has these four things is a stream-enterer, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.”
That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
segs.e: Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:
“Whoever has faith in the Realized One,
unwavering and well grounded;
whose ethical conduct is good,
praised and loved by the noble ones;
who has confidence in the Saṅgha,
and correct view:
they’re said to be prosperous,
their life is not in vain.
So let the wise devote themselves
to faith, ethical behaviour,
confidence, and insight into the teaching,
remembering the instructions of the Buddhas.”
Linked Discourses 55.52
6. A Wise Person
One Who Completed the Rains

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro bhikkhu sāvatthiyaṁ vassaṁvuttho kapilavatthuṁ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena.
segs.e: Now at that time a certain mendicant who had completed the rainy season residence in Sāvatthī arrived at Kapilavatthu on some business.

segs.p: Assosuṁ kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā: “aññataro kira bhikkhu sāvatthiyaṁ vassaṁvuttho kapilavatthuṁ anuppatto”ti.
segs.e: The Sakyans of Kapilavatthu heard about this.

segs.p: Atha kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā yena so bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā taṁ bhikkhuṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho kāpilavatthavā sakyā taṁ bhikkhuṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: They went to that mendicant, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

segs.p: “kacci, bhante, bhagavā arogo ceva balavā cā”ti?
segs.e: “Sir, we hope that the Buddha is healthy and strong.”
“He is, respectable sirs.”

segs.p: “Kacci pana, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā arogā ceva balavanto cā”ti?
segs.e: “And we hope that Sāriputta and Moggallāna are healthy and strong.”

segs.p: “Sāriputtamoggallānāpi kho, āvuso, arogā ceva balavanto cā”ti.
segs.e: “They are.”

segs.p: “Kacci pana, bhante, bhikkhusaṅgho arogo ca balavā cā”ti.
segs.e: “And we hope that the mendicant Saṅgha is healthy and strong.”

segs.p: “Bhikkhusaṅghopi kho, āvuso, arogo ca balavā cā”ti.
segs.e: “It is.”

segs.p: “Atthi pana te, bhante, kiñci iminā antaravassena bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitan”ti?
segs.e: “But sir, during this rains residence did you hear and learn anything in the presence of the Buddha?”

segs.p: “Sammukhā metaṁ, āvuso, bhagavato sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: “Respectable sirs, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye āsavānaṁ khayā anāsavaṁ cetovimuttiṁ paññāvimuttiṁ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṁ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharanti.
segs.e: ‘There are fewer mendicants who realize the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom, and live having realized it with their own insight in this very life due to the ending of defilements.

segs.p: Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū ye pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā’ti.
segs.e: There are more mendicants who, having ended the five lower fetters, are reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.’

segs.p: Aparampi kho me, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: In addition, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā opapātikā tattha parinibbāyino anāvattidhammā tasmā lokā.
segs.e: ‘There are fewer mendicants who, having ended the five lower fetters, are reborn spontaneously, and will be extinguished there, not liable to return from that world.

segs.p: Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū ye tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karissantī’ti.
segs.e: There are more mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, who come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.’

segs.p: Aparampi kho me, āvuso, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ:
segs.e: In addition, I heard and learned this in the presence of the Buddha:

segs.p: ‘appakā te, bhikkhave, bhikkhū ye tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā rāgadosamohānaṁ tanuttā sakadāgāmino, sakideva imaṁ lokaṁ āgantvā dukkhassantaṁ karissanti.
segs.e: ‘There are fewer mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters, and the weakening of greed, hate, and delusion, are once-returners, who come back to this world once only, then make an end of suffering.

segs.p: Atha kho eteva bahutarā bhikkhū ye tiṇṇaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā sotāpannā avinipātadhammā niyatā sambodhiparāyaṇā’”ti.
segs.e: There are more mendicants who, with the ending of three fetters are stream-enterers, not liable to be reborn in the underworld, assured, destined for awakening.’”
Linked Discourses 55.53
6. A Wise Person
With Dhammadinna

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā bārāṇasiyaṁ viharati isipatane migadāye.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Varanasi in the deer park at Isipatana.

segs.p: Atha kho dhammadinno upāsako pañcahi upāsakasatehi saddhiṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho dhammadinno upāsako bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then the lay follower Dhammadinna, together with five hundred lay followers, went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:
“May the Buddha please advise

segs.p: anusāsatu no, bhante, bhagavā yaṁ amhākaṁ assa dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāyā”ti.
segs.e: and instruct us. It will be for our lasting welfare and happiness.”
“So, Dhammadinna, you should all train like this:

segs.p: ‘ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatapaṭisaṁyuttā te kālena kālaṁ upasampajja viharissāmā’ti.
segs.e: ‘From time to time we will undertake and dwell upon the discourses spoken by the Realized One that are deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness.’
That’s how you should train yourselves.”

segs.p: “Na kho netaṁ, bhante, sukaraṁ amhehi puttasambādhasayanaṁ ajjhāvasantehi kāsikacandanaṁ paccanubhontehi mālāgandhavilepanaṁ dhārayantehi jātarūparajataṁ sādiyantehi—
segs.e: “Sir, we live at home with our children, using sandalwood imported from Kāsi, wearing garlands, fragrance, and makeup, and accepting gold and currency.

segs.p: ye te suttantā tathāgatabhāsitā gambhīrā gambhīratthā lokuttarā suññatapaṭisaṁyuttā te kālena kālaṁ upasampajja viharituṁ.
segs.e: It’s not easy for us to undertake and dwell from time to time upon the discourses spoken by the Realized One that are deep, profound, transcendent, dealing with emptiness.

segs.p: Tesaṁ no, bhante, bhagavā amhākaṁ pañcasu sikkhāpadesu ṭhitānaṁ uttaridhammaṁ desetū”ti.
segs.e: Since we are established in the five training rules, please teach us further.”
“So, Dhammadinna, you should all train like this:
‘We will have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …

segs.p: ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgatā bhavissāma akhaṇḍehi …pe… samādhisaṁvattanikehī’ti.
segs.e: And we will have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.’
That’s how you should train yourselves.”

segs.p: “Yānimāni, bhante, bhagavatā cattāri sotāpattiyaṅgāni desitāni, saṁvijjante dhammā amhesu, mayañca tesu dhammesu sandissāma.
segs.e: “Sir, these four factors of stream-entry that were taught by the Buddha are found in us, and we embody them.
For we have experiential confidence in the Buddha …

segs.p: itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.

segs.e: the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
And we have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.”
“You’re all fortunate, Dhammadinna, so very fortunate!
You’ve all declared the fruit of stream-entry.”
Linked Discourses 55.54
6. A Wise Person
Sick

segs.p: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Sakyans, near Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū bhagavato cīvarakammaṁ karonti:
segs.e: At that time several mendicants were making a robe for the Buddha, thinking that
when his robe was finished and the three months of the rains residence had passed the Buddha would set out wandering.
Mahānāma the Sakyan heard about this.

segs.p: Atha kho mahānāmo sakko yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahānāmo sakko bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
segs.e: Then he went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and told him that he had heard that the Buddha was leaving. He added,

segs.p: Na kho netaṁ, bhante, bhagavato sammukhā sutaṁ sammukhā paṭiggahitaṁ
segs.e: “Sir, I haven’t heard and learned it in the presence of the Buddha

segs.p: sappaññena upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno ovaditabbo”ti.
segs.e: how a wise lay follower should advise another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill.”

segs.p: “Sappaññena, mahānāma, upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno catūhi assāsanīyehi dhammehi assāsetabbo:
segs.e: “Mahānāma, a wise lay follower should put at ease another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill with four consolations.
‘Be at ease, sir.

segs.p: atthāyasmato buddhe aveccappasādo itipi so bhagavā …pe… satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavāti.
segs.e: You have experiential confidence in the Buddha …
the teaching …
the Saṅgha …
And you have the ethical conduct loved by the noble ones … leading to immersion.’

segs.p: Sappaññena, mahānāma, upāsakena sappañño upāsako ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno imehi catūhi assāsanīyehi dhammehi assāsetvā evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: When a wise lay follower has put at ease another wise lay follower who is sick, suffering, gravely ill with these four consolations, they should say:
‘Are you concerned for your mother and father?’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘atthi me mātāpitūsu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I am,’ they should say:
‘But sir, it’s your nature to die.
Whether or not you are concerned for your mother and father,

segs.p: no cepāyasmā mātāpitūsu apekkhaṁ karissati, marissateva.
segs.e: you will die anyway.

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, yā te mātāpitūsu apekkhā taṁ pajahā’ti.
segs.e: It would be good to give up concern for your mother and father.’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘yā me mātāpitūsu apekkhā sā pahīnā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I have given up concern for my mother and father,’ they should say:
‘But are you concerned for your partners and children?’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘atthi me puttadāresu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I am,’ they should say:
‘But sir, it’s your nature to die.
Whether or not you are concerned for your partners and children,

segs.p: no cepāyasmā puttadāresu apekkhaṁ karissati, marissateva.
segs.e: you will die anyway.

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, yā te puttadāresu apekkhā taṁ pajahā’ti.
segs.e: It would be good to give up concern for your partners and children.’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘yā me puttadāresu apekkhā sā pahīnā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I have given up concern for my partners and children,’ they should say:
‘But are you concerned for the five kinds of human sensual stimulation?’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘atthi me mānusakesu pañcasu kāmaguṇesu apekkhā’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I am,’ they should say:

segs.p: ‘mānusakehi kho, āvuso, kāmehi dibbā kāmā abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā ca.
segs.e: ‘Respectable sir, heavenly sensual pleasures are better than human sensual pleasures.

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, mānusakehi kāmehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā cātumahārājikesu devesu cittaṁ adhimocehī’ti.
segs.e: It would be good to turn your mind away from human sensual pleasures and focus it on the gods of the four great kings.’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘mānusakehi me kāmehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ, cātumahārājikesu devesu cittaṁ adhimocitan’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I have done so,’ they should say:

segs.p: ‘cātumahārājikehi kho, āvuso, devehi tāvatiṁsā devā abhikkantatarā ca paṇītatarā ca.
segs.e: ‘Respectable sir, the gods of the thirty-three are better than the gods of the four great kings …

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, cātumahārājikehi devehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā tāvatiṁsesu devesu cittaṁ adhimocehī’ti.
‘cātumahārājikehi me devehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ, tāvatiṁsesu devesu cittaṁ adhimocitan’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:

segs.e: Respectable sir, the gods of Yama …
the joyful gods …
the gods who love to create …
the gods who control what is created by others …

segs.p: paranimmitavasavattīhi kho, āvuso, devehi brahmaloko abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca.
segs.e: the gods of the realm of divinity are better than the gods who control what is created by others.

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, paranimmitavasavattīhi devehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā brahmaloke cittaṁ adhimocehī’ti.
segs.e: It would be good to turn your mind away from the gods who control what is created by others and focus it on the gods of the realm of divinity.’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘paranimmitavasavattīhi me devehi cittaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ, brahmaloke cittaṁ adhimocitan’ti, so evamassa vacanīyo:
segs.e: ‘I have done so,’ they should say:
‘Respectable sir, the realm of divinity is impermanent, not lasting, and included within substantial reality.

segs.p: Sādhāyasmā, brahmalokā cittaṁ vuṭṭhāpetvā sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ upasaṁharāhī’ti.
segs.e: It would be good to turn your mind away from the realm of divinity and apply it to the cessation of substantial reality.’
If they reply,

segs.p: ‘brahmalokā me cittaṁ vuṭṭhitaṁ, sakkāyanirodhe cittaṁ upasaṁharāmī’ti;
segs.e: ‘I have done so,’

segs.p: evaṁ vimuttacittassa kho, mahānāma, upāsakassa āsavā vimuttacittena bhikkhunā na kiñci nānākaraṇaṁ vadāmi, yadidaṁ—
segs.e: then there is no difference between a lay follower whose mind is freed in this way and a mendicant whose mind is freed from defilements; that is,
between the freedom of one and the other.”
Linked Discourses 55.55
6. A Wise Person
The Fruit of Stream-Entry

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when four things are developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.
What four?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When these four things are developed and cultivated they lead to the realization of the fruit of stream-entry.”

7. Great Wisdom
Great Wisdom

segs.p: “Cattārome, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahāpaññatāya saṁvattanti.
segs.e: “Mendicants, when four things are developed and cultivated they lead to great wisdom.
What four?

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahāpaññatāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When these four things are developed and cultivated they lead to great wisdom.”

Penetrating Wisdom
“Mendicants, when four things are developed and cultivated they lead to penetrating wisdom.
What four?
Associating with true persons, listening to the true teaching, rational application of mind, and practicing in line with the teaching.

segs.p: ime kho, bhikkhave, cattāro dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā nibbedhikapaññatāya saṁvattantī”ti.
segs.e: When these four things are developed and cultivated they lead to penetrating wisdom.”
